he step up into the Park Ridge home makes
Sam Biardo Sr. look even bigger as he comes
to the door. A burly bear of a man, he looks
solid, the kind of man young kids flock around on a
soccer field in order to feel safe. But as he turns away
from you to enter the room, you catch sight of his eyes
and you know, in some innate way, that that is what
grief looks like - that dark flooding color that flits
across in a ghostly pass, a momentary hint of the merciless prowler that, anywhere, any moment, could easily
fell even a big man like him.
He is unfailingly polite but uneasy, and we both
know why.The tape recorder and yellow pad set out on
the table look harmless, but they threaten to once again
eviscerate him as he talks about the loss of his son. But
he will tell me later, though he is not a religious man,
" The church has the right idea. ... They celebrate life,
and they celebrate death.You've got to do it."
And so this is what Mary and Sam Biardo are
doing -learning to celebrate the life of their son,
doing his young life justice by memorializing all that
was good.

And some of those close to Sam are starting to

" The way Sam led his life -with what happened,

In their own attempts to work through their grief,
the Biardos have actively tried to heal - through counseling, books, the compassion of friends, accepting
change, being open with their feelings and realizing the
futility of avoidance.
" For us to sit back and just vegetate," Mary
contemplated, " I don't think that celebrates his life
in any way."
" We're happy that we had 19 V2 years," she said.
" We're better people for it, so let's show it."
But to understand the enormous recovery the
Biardos have striven for following their son's passing,
consider Mary's chilling comparison of the events of
9/11 with the death of a child:
" If you want to understand a little bit more of
what it feels like [to have a child die], think of yourself
as one of those towers, and think of the jet just coming
into your chest, smoldering, exploding, and then you
crumble.There's chaos, people saying,'Oh, everyone's
going to be all right.' No, everyone's not going to be all
right."
But somehow, the Biardos and the brothers of Psi
Upsilon have worked together and managed to become
just a little bit better.
" [The situation] is extremely rare," Reed said,
"and points to the coming together of an extraordinary
family and extraordinary young men."

Mission Statement
STRATEGIC
PLAN
The mission of Psi Upsilon is to promote and encourage:
The union of undergraduate and alumni members for the
development of the highest moral, intellectual, and social
excellence;
The commitment of its members to a diverse brotherhood of
firm and enduring friendship that will last a lifetime;
Development of planning, organization, and leadership skills;
and,
A spirit of service and commitment to fraternity, college, and
community.
Psi Upsilon Fraternity Strategic Issues Plan
Our Vision for Psi Upsilon
It is our vision for Psi Upsilon that it uill he a fraternity of about 50 chapters found at selective
and highly selective North American institutions of higher education whose undergraduate and
alumni members are dedicated to the development of moral, intellectual, and social excellence
in a fellowship of mutual respect and regard that honors diversity in its chapters and members.
Goals
IV. Ritual
Goal: Study, modify, and create ritual to reflect and
reinforce a vision of Psi Upsilon consistent with its
mission statement, and the educational programs of the
Fraternity.
I. Recruitment
Goal: Ensure that the number of members in each
chapter, and in Psi Upsilon overall, is adequate to meet
the needs and responsibilities appropriate for the
operations and leadership of each chapter; participation
in and financial obligations of membership in the
International Fraternity and the IFC; and to ensure
sustained membership over time.
V. Development
Goal: Secure, develop, and preserve, financial,
board, and staff resources to implement the strategic
plan and to maintain the quality and scope of existing
programs and services.
II. Educational Programming
Goal: Develop and implement an educational
program that is consistent with and reinforces
principles expressed in Psi Upsilon s mission statement. VI. Expansion
Goal: Implement the current plan and establish 4050 chapters by 2008-10.
III. Governance
Goal: Provide effective, efficient, and strategic
governance of Psi Upsilon.
